news.title: After Brazil, India to Face Another FIFA World Cup 2026 Team? Report Makes Big Claim
news.lede: On October 3, India and Brazil shall face each other for the first time ever. The match is going to be played in Kolkata. Now it seems that India may play another country that took part in the FIFA World Cup 2026. This side made its debut and went as far as the Round of 32 and also held eventual champions Spain to a goalless draw in the group stage.

news.title: Socceroos’ World Cup heroics trigger $100m transfer bonanza
news.lede: The Socceroos may have only made it to the first round of the knockouts at the FIFA World Cup, but it was enough to impress some of the biggest clubs in Europe. On Wednesday morning (AEST), news broke Portuguese club Benfica was on the verge of signing defender Alessandro Circati on a $33 million deal. Alessandro Circati is on the verge of signing a monster deal with Porguguese club Benfica. Should the deal be signed, sealed and delivered, it would take the total transfer fees paid for Australian stars well beyond $100 million.

news.title: FIFA accused of 'management by fear' after key executive's sudden exit
news.lede: Lise Klaveness (right) has issued a blistering criticism of FIFA following the exit of a senior official. (Getty Images: Eva Marie Uzcategui). Lise Klaveness, the head of Norwegian football, believes FIFA is exhibiting "management by fear" after the exit of COO Kevin Lamour. Lamour was one of the FIFA executives who was outspoken against president Gianni Infantino's controversial plan to sell off the World Cup.

news.title: Senegal Name World Cup Winner Patrick Vieira New Head Coach
news.lede: Senegal have appointed former France international Patrick Vieira as their new head coach, with the 1998 World Cup winner replacing Pape Thiaw, who was sacked following the country’s disappointing World Cup campaign. The Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) confirmed Vieira’s appointment on Tuesday, describing the decision as a “strategic move” aimed…... The Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) confirmed Vieira’s appointment on Tuesday, describing the decision as a “strategic move” aimed at strengthening the national team’s technical structure. The federation said the appointment was intended to “establish a high-level technical staff, in line with our country’s sporting ambitions”.

news.title: WATCH: Squad set for tough group challenge at FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: Members of the New Zealand squad are ‘ready for the challenge’ of playing at September’s FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland. “We’ve been drawn into a very competitive group,” says head coach Callum Holmes. “Japan, Italy and the United States are all strong football nations with different strengths and styles of play, so every match will present a unique challenge. Starting against Japan for the second consecutive tournament gives us a familiar benchmark, and we know we’ll need to be at our very best if we’re going to progress.”

news.title: Jamaica ready to co-host 2031 FIFA Women’s World Cup
news.lede: The Jamaican Government and Jamaica Football Federation (JFF) signed guarantee agreements recently, marking a major step towards co-hosting the 2031 FIFA Women’s World Cup. Minister of Culture, Gender, Entertainment and Sport Olivia Grange, together with JFF President Michael Ricketts, both signed the agreement which commits both entities to working with FIFA as the country prepares to host the tournament alongside the United States, Costa Rica and Mexico. “With the signing, the Government of Jamaica and the Jamaica Football Federation will partner with FIFA in fulfilling the responsibilities and deliverables associated with Jamaica’s hosting obligations. These include establishing legal mechanisms for guarantees, bonds, declarations,” Grange said at the signing ceremony.

news.title: AP Interview: Klaveness slams Infantino’s FIFA for firing top executive in ‘management by fear’
news.lede: GENEVA (AP) — Norway’s soccer federation president on Tuesday accused FIFA of fear tactics for the removal of a senior official who publicly opposed FIFA leader Gianni Infantino’s now-withdrawn World Cup sell-off plan. Lise Klaveness, who heads the Norwegian Football Federation since 2022, told The Associated Press that the firing of FIFA’s chief operating officer Kevin Lamour was “unacceptable” and urged other senior leaders to resist potentially damaging orders. Lamour’s exit late Monday came 17 days after his statement to AP criticizing Infantino’s $20 billion private equity project, which was withdrawn just hours later. “Now he is thrown out and we are supposed to move on.
